title: Dispatch GID 2: Audience Sees Many Worlds and Hears One Warning
summary: The inventor calls the shared voice evidence that his apparatus reached a single place.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: The Concordance Instrument was unveiled last evening. When its silvered plate was raised, spectators reported widely different scenes. A surveyor saw a river flowing upward through a stone arch. Miss Agnes Morrow saw the municipal archive empty of books. A boy in the gallery saw a field of small, dark chairs. Dr. Saye, seated near the front, said she saw the Lyceum as if from a seat across the aisle.

Almost everyone heard the same voice: “Turn it off.” It spoke twice, quietly, while the lamp was still burning. The warning is present on a phonographic cylinder placed beside the plate. There is no agreement about its source. Dr. Halden says it demonstrates that the different views belong to a single region with shared sound.

Miss Marsh shut the instrument after six minutes. Several spectators objected; others had already moved toward the doors. Mabel Crain, posted at the rear aisle, was seen checking the exits while the plate was raised. She told an usher afterward that she heard the warning before the audience did.

Halden dismissed suggestions that the voice was a staged effect. He offered Dr. Saye the cylinder and invited the Institute to examine the lamp, lenses, and plate. “If something there wishes to speak,” he said, “that is surely the discovery we came to make.”

The Lyceum closed after the audience departed. This morning its manager found one chair warm and indented although the ticket for it had never been sold. He has asked the Institute to inspect the auditorium before a second showing is arranged.
